matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value and compute the numeric discrepancy between the two sides (or between the current result and the target equality).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When first analyzing the puzzle, before generating any stick moves.
matchstick.example: Not computing that IV = 4 and XVII + XIV = 31, so the needed adjustment of -27 is missed.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Enumerate every way a single matchstick can be relocated from any character (including operators) to any other character, respecting the orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) of the sticks.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the discrepancy, to generate the set of candidate moves.
matchstick.example: Overlooking the move that takes the vertical stick from '+' and adds it as a new I to XVII.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, calculate how the numeric values of the affected numerals and operators change and check whether the combined effect equals the previously computed discrepancy.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During evaluation of each candidate move, to check if its numeric effect matches the required discrepancy.
matchstick.example: Treating the change of '+' to '-' as a -14 adjustment instead of the correct -28 (twice the term).

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A '+' consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into '-', and adding a vertical stick to '-' creates a '+'. Use this to switch addition to subtraction (or vice‑versa) with a single stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a candidate move involves the '+' operator and a vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal stick from '+' (which doesn't have one) and creating an invalid operator.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If adding a stick to a numeral changes its value by the needed amount, move a stick from an operator (or another character) to that numeral, ensuring the source operator remains a valid symbol after removal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a stick can be taken from an operator and added to a numeral to adjust its value, while keeping the operator valid.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' to a numeral but leaving '+' as a lone horizontal line, which is not a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Equation structure preservation
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must still contain exactly one '=', each side must have at least one valid numeral, and all operators must remain valid symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After applying a stick move, before checking numeric equality, to ensure the equation still has exactly one '=', and both sides contain valid numerals and operators.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from '=', leaving the equation without any equality sign.

matchstick.title: Known single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: Use a lookup of common single‑stick numeral changes (e.g., X↔V, I↔V, I↔X) and their associated numeric changes (±5, ±4, ±9) to quickly evaluate candidate moves.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering possible changes to numerals, include these standard single‑stick transformations as candidates.
matchstick.example: Changing X to V by removing a diagonal stick, resulting in a single diagonal that is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting Roman numerals
matchstick.principle: After any stick move that alters a numeral (or operator), verify that the resulting character follows standard Roman numeral syntax (or is a valid operator). Discard any transformation that leaves an invalid character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any stick move, before accepting the solution, verify that all altered characters are valid Roman numerals or operators.
matchstick.example: After moving a stick from X, the remaining shape is a single diagonal, failing Roman numeral validation.

matchstick.title: Maintain exactly one equality sign after stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from the '=', ensure the source becomes a valid operator (e.g., '-' after losing a horizontal stick) and that another operator receives the stick to become '=', preserving exactly one equality sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the '=' sign is involved in the stick move, ensure the source becomes a valid operator and another operator receives the stick to become '=', preserving a single equality sign.
matchstick.example: Taking a horizontal stick from '=', turning it into '-', but not adding it to another operator, so the equation ends up with no '=' sign.

matchstick.title: Operator sign change impact
matchstick.principle: When a stick move changes an operator (e.g., '+' to '-'), account for the sign reversal of the term in the numeric impact calculation; the term's contribution changes from +value to -value (or vice‑versa), which is a net change of twice the term's value.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During numeric impact calculation, if the operator changes, incorporate the resulting sign reversal of the term into the net numeric change.
matchstick.example: Ignoring that converting '+' to '-' flips the sign of the term, so the net numeric change is miscalculated.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a numeral or operator without checking that the remaining shape still corresponds to a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After moving a stick, verify that both the source and destination characters are still valid symbols; only remove sticks from characters that remain valid after removal.

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes a transformation yields a correct equation without actually computing the numeric values of both sides.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recompute the integer values of the left and right sides after applying a stick move and confirm they are equal.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: In the process of moving sticks, the model accidentally deletes or forgets characters, breaking the equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Maintain the full sequence of characters; when moving a stick, keep all original characters present, only altering their shapes.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: When an operator is altered (e.g., '+' to '-'), the model does not account for the resulting sign reversal of the term in the arithmetic.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When evaluating a stick move that changes an operator, include the sign change in the numeric impact calculation (the term's contribution changes by twice its value).

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model either adds or removes sticks instead of moving exactly one, violating the puzzle constraints.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure that exactly one stick is relocated: remove it from a source character and place it on a destination character, without adding or deleting any sticks.
